_comment: The voice-health dataset landscape, as a machine-readable registry.
This is the SINGLE SOURCE for docs/datasets.html -- the page is generated, never
hand-edited, so no number on it can drift from this file (CLAUDE.md R1/R2).
'claim' is this program's own judgement of what a dataset can support HERE, and is
the column that does not exist in any published survey:
EVALUATION -- real speaker ids AND enough speakers to clear the rigor contract
SCREENING  -- speaker-disjoint is possible but n is too small for an external claim
BLOCKED    -- obtainable in principle, not obtained (paperwork, gate, or DUA)
NEVER      -- a structural defect means it may never carry a generalisation claim
Every arXiv id below was fetched and its title+authors confirmed before it shipped.
'[UNVERIFIED]' marks anything that failed a fetch. Never cite from memory.
generated_note: counts are quoted from the cited source, not measured here, unless the dataset appears in data/interim/

families.name: Voice & larynx pathology
families.mechanism: The sound-producing organ itself is altered -- paralysis, polyp, oedema, tumour, surgical scarring. The shortest causal chain in the field and where the evidence is strongest.

datasets.name: SVD (Saarbrücken Voice Database)
datasets.tasks: /a/ /i/ /u/ at 4 pitch conditions + one sentence + EGG
datasets.claim_note: THE PRIMARY TARGET. Real speaker ids, 1,679 decoded here. But only 12 of the 71 pathologies have ≥30 speakers and 19 have exactly one — so the powered task is binary, not 71-way.

datasets.name: Bridge2AI-Voice v3.1.0
datasets.conditions: 5 cohorts incl. voice disorders, neuro, mood, respiratory, pediatric
datasets.tasks: sustained vowels, read + spontaneous speech, cough, breathing
datasets.access: credentialed + signed DUA; raw audio needs a separate DACO application
datasets.sota: VoiceFM contrastive baseline (medRxiv 2026.05.28); laryngeal-lesion model, Front. Digit. Health 2026
datasets.claim_note: The most ambitious purpose-built corpus in the field. PhysioNet tier ships DERIVED FEATURES ONLY (spectrograms/MFCC/PPG) — raw audio is a second committee. Paperwork-bound, not compute-bound.

datasets.name: RRP-Voice
datasets.n: longitudinal, per-subject follow-up up to 10 years
datasets.labels: synchronous laryngoscopic ground truth at each visit
datasets.claim_note: Unusually strong labels — an endoscopic look at the larynx at every recording, which almost no corpus has. But longitudinal repeats mean subject leakage is near-guaranteed under naive splits.

datasets.name: VOICED
datasets.claim_note: Small and single-vowel, but open and in a different language from SVD — which makes it the natural cross-corpus destination for an SVD-trained model.

datasets.name: PVQD (Perceptual Voice Qualities Database)
datasets.claim_note: Severity ratings rather than diagnosis, and studio conditions make results optimistic. Useful as a regression target, not a detection benchmark.

families.name: Parkinson's & motor-neurological
families.mechanism: Speech needs fine neuromuscular control, so hypokinetic dysarthria appears early in PD. A longer causal chain than the larynx family but a well-replicated one.

datasets.name: PC-GITA
datasets.claim_note: n=100 is far below this program's floor. Its value is the metadata: PC-GITA and NeuroVoz are the only two corpora carrying enough staging detail to isolate EARLY-stage PD.

datasets.name: NeuroVoz
datasets.sota: shares the EarlyPD benchmark with PC-GITA
datasets.claim_note: ON-medication state only, so it cannot separate disease from treatment response. Pairs with PC-GITA for a Spanish cross-corpus test.

datasets.name: mPower
datasets.n: tens of thousands of voice tasks, longitudinal smartphone cohort
datasets.claim_note: By far the largest PD voice cohort, and the most dangerous: self-report labels plus heavy repeated measures per participant. Reported accuracies here have historically collapsed once splits were made subject-disjoint.

datasets.name: MDVR-KCL
datasets.claim_note: Mobile-device capture makes it a realistic acquisition-shift partner for studio-recorded PD corpora.

families.name: Dementia, MCI & cognition
families.mechanism: Language production degrades before motor speech does, so the signal is as much linguistic (word-finding, semantic density) as acoustic. This is why text models beat audio models here — and why the shortcut risk is highest.

datasets.name: PROCESS-2
datasets.tasks: semantic + phonemic fluency, Cookie Theft (+ manual transcripts)
datasets.labels: NHS memory-service diagnosis; MMSE for only 174/400
datasets.claim_note: The highest-headroom cognitive task available (macro-F1 0.59 leaves real room). But 400 participants fails the ≥500/class bar and MMSE is missing for 56.5%.

datasets.name: ADReSS / ADReSSo / ADReSS-M / TAUKADIAL
datasets.n: ~156 subjects (ADReSS), balanced for age and sex BY DESIGN
datasets.sota: F-score ~0.79 (with age+sex as inputs); ADReSSo acoustic ~0.76
datasets.claim_note: The one family that already age- and sex-matches by design — the correct response to the confound this program studies. Note the headline uses age+sex AS INPUTS, so it is not a confound-free number either. Balancing removes age/sex; session, administration and transcription effects remain.

datasets.name: PARLO Dementia Corpus
datasets.claim_note: Non-English dementia corpora are rare; multi-centre design means site effects must be measured, not assumed away.

families.name: Dysarthria & motor speech
families.mechanism: Direct motor impairment of articulation from PD, ALS, cerebral palsy, stroke. Severity, not diagnosis, is usually the target.

datasets.name: SAP (Speech Accessibility Project)
datasets.conditions: dysarthria: Parkinson's, ALS, cerebral palsy, stroke, Down syndrome
datasets.claim_note: THE POSITIVE EXAMPLE of the whole survey: explicitly designed for speaker-INDEPENDENT evaluation, at a scale nothing else in this table reaches. If more corpora were built this way, this program would have less to audit.

datasets.name: TORGO / UASpeech
datasets.claim_note: 15 and 19 speakers with thousands of utterances each. Any random split leaks speaker identity almost surely; the reported accuracies are largely speaker-recognition. Not a generalisation benchmark at any n.

families.name: Respiratory & infectious
families.mechanism: Airway obstruction and inflammation change cough and breath acoustics. Also the field's canonical cautionary tale — see the UK ONS row.

datasets.name: Coswara
datasets.claim_note: Real participant ids, so speaker-disjoint splits are possible — but the returning-user flag is missing for 680 of 2,746, making it submission-disjoint rather than person-disjoint. Intra-dataset AUC ~0.92 collapses cross-corpus.

datasets.name: COUGHVID
datasets.claim_note: PERMANENTLY DEMOTED HERE. 13,535 decoded rows, 13,535 unique uuids, ZERO participant identifiers. A 'speaker-disjoint' split over recording uuids is not speaker-disjoint, and there is no way to detect the violation. Pretraining and OOD probing only.

datasets.name: UK ONS / Turing vocal audio
datasets.labels: PCR-REFERENCED — the strongest labels in the family
datasets.sota: AUC 0.846 unadjusted → 0.619 after matching on confounders
datasets.claim_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THIS TABLE. The largest, best-labelled respiratory corpus ever built, and when its authors matched on recruitment confounders the headline fell from 0.846 to 0.619. That single number is the empirical case for this entire program.

datasets.name: ICBHI 2017 respiratory sound
datasets.claim_note: Event-level, not nosological — it detects a sound, not a disease. Fixed equipment per site makes device a near-perfect site proxy.

families.name: Mental health
families.mechanism: Prosody, pause structure and speaking rate shift with mood state. The weakest causal chain in the field, and the one where interview-protocol artifacts do the most damage.

datasets.name: DAIC-WOZ / E-DAIC (AVEC)
datasets.claim_note: The interviewer-prompt shortcut: the questions asked of depressed participants differ, so a model can score well by classifying the INTERVIEWER. Audited again in 2026 (arXiv:2605.23977) with worse news — see below.

datasets.name: CMDC / ANDROIDS / MODMA / PDCH
datasets.claim_note: The 2026 multi-probe audit found models strong on CMDC and ANDROIDS fail to transfer zero-shot, and that text beats audio consistently across all five seeds — i.e. these benchmarks are measuring interview content, not voice.

datasets.name: Voice Biomarkers for Depression & Anxiety
datasets.access: DATA PROPRIETARY; model released on HuggingFace
datasets.claim_note: By far the largest mental-health voice cohort ever reported — and the data is not released, so the 71% cannot be audited by anyone. The released model is usable; the claim is not checkable.

families.name: Multi-phenotype & cross-cutting benchmarks
families.mechanism: Rather than one disease, these ask what a single voice sample carries across many conditions at once — the honest version of the 'voice as a vital sign' claim.

datasets.name: SpeechDx
datasets.conditions: 27 tasks across 12 datasets, organised by speech-production stage (conceptualization / formulation / articulation)
datasets.sota: large-scale speech models are the strongest overall baselines
datasets.claim_note: THE MOST IMPORTANT NEW RELEASE for this program. Its headline conclusion is that NO current representation generalises reliably across the clinical speech landscape — independent, and from a different direction, of what F3 found here. Its production-stage taxonomy is also the right way to organise this table.

datasets.name: HPP-Voice
datasets.conditions: 15 phenotypes across 6 systems: sleep apnea, insomnia, asthma, smoking, sinusitis, anemia, thyroid, migraine, depression, anxiety, COVID, allergy …
datasets.sota: sleep apnea (males) AUC 0.64 ± 0.03 vs MFCC 0.56 vs DEMOGRAPHIC BASELINE 0.57
datasets.claim_note: THE REALISM CHECK. The only large study in this table that reports a demographic baseline next to its headline — and once it does, the best effect is 0.64 against a 0.57 bar. That is what an honest voice-phenotype effect size looks like.

datasets.name: RespiraMFM
datasets.claim_note: Multimodal by design — it fuses audio with patient history and symptoms. Worth flagging that adding symptoms to a respiratory model is exactly the confound the UK ONS study isolated; the gain must be attributed carefully.

datasets.name: Voice EHR
datasets.claim_note: Represents the collection-protocol direction: build the corpus around the health record rather than retrofitting labels onto found audio.

meta_studies.name: SpeechDx: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Clinical Speech AI
meta_studies.authors: Bhalla, Kieu, Merchant, de Lara, Mariakakis
meta_studies.why: 27 tasks over 12 datasets. Concludes NO current representation generalises reliably across clinical speech — converging with this program's F3 from a completely different direction.

meta_studies.name: A Multi-Probe Audit of Clinical-Interview Depression Detection Benchmarks
meta_studies.why: The closest published work to this program's method. Audits DAIC/E-DAIC, CMDC, ANDROIDS, MODMA, PDCH and finds the official E-DAIC leaderboard is essentially noise: the best CV configuration ranks 20th on the official test, the test winner ranks 41st by CV, and top-3 overlap is ZERO. Text beats audio on symptom-dense segments across all seeds.

meta_studies.name: Systematic FAIRness Assessment of Open Voice Biomarker Datasets
meta_studies.why: Scores 27 public voice-biomarker datasets on FAIR maturity. Findability is uniformly high; accessibility, interoperability and reusability vary wildly. Explains why half the rows above say BLOCKED.

meta_studies.name: Vocal audio for COVID-19 screening (UK ONS / Turing)
meta_studies.why: AUC 0.846 unadjusted → 0.619 after matching on recruitment confounders, on 67,842 PCR-referenced individuals. The single strongest empirical justification for measuring the margin above a confound baseline.
